body_markdown:
Gamified email capture usually ends in a coupon. The wheel spins, the shopper gets 10% off, and the list fills with people who won’t buy without one. Playably builds the same games without the code, and the opt-in rates hold.


Three campaigns give the numbers: Roshambo Eyewear at an 8.2% opt-in rate, My Medic at 3,659 opt-ins and a 227% lift, and Skout at 7× ROI with 200+ survey responses.


Playably is the best option for brands that want a list of full-price buyers, because the game is the reward and no code waits at the end.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Gamified email capture doesn’t need a discount to work.** Playably’s games trade a code for a game worth playing.
- **Roshambo recorded an 8.2% opt-in rate** against a 4.35% benchmark, with a 20.38% game start rate.
- **My Medic lifted opt-in rate from 0.92% to 3.02%** between two versions of the same game, a 227% improvement.
- **Skout returned 7× ROI and 4× email conversion** from a survey game that also collected product feedback.
- **The list quality differs.** A no-code list is full-price buyers; a coupon list is discount hunters.


## **Why gamified email capture usually ends in a coupon**


A 10%-off pop-up works, which is why every store has one.


What it builds is a list conditioned to expect a code. The first purchase is discounted, the second waits for the next sale, and reactivation costs another discount. You’ve paid for the email twice before the customer is profitable.


There’s also the volume problem. Pop-ups are ignored at scale, which is why brands keep raising the offer from 10% to 15% to 20% to hold the same opt-in rate.


## **Three campaigns, three mechanics**


All three ran on Playably, and none of them ended in a discount code.


### **Roshambo Eyewear: a play-to-win game replacing pop-ups**


Roshambo swapped its pop-up for a Playably game in a campaign that ran under three weeks in November 2025.


Results from the[Roshambo case study](https://playably.ai/pages/roshambo-eyewear) :


- 8.2% opt-in rate, against a 4.35% benchmark for pop-up tools
- 20.38% game start rate, roughly double the benchmark cited on the page
- 66.62% completion rate
- 6× ROI and $15,277 in revenue


#### **Why the start rate matters more than the opt-in rate**


Opt-in rate measures the offer. Start rate measures whether the thing looked worth doing. A high start rate with a low completion rate means the game is too long; the reverse means the invitation is weak.


### **My Medic: a game iterated into a 227% lift**


My Medic ran a Playably “Rescue Simulator” over July and August 2025, with the score reveal gated behind an opt-in.


From the[My Medic case study](https://playably.ai/pages/my-medic) :


- 3,659 email and SMS opt-ins from 121,000 impressions
- Opt-in rate up from 0.92% to 3.02% between versions, a 227% lift
- Completion up from 30.7% to 48.9%
- 4× ROI


The lesson is that version one underperformed. The gain came from shortening the game and moving the gate.


### **Skout: a survey game that captured data, not just emails**


Skout’s Playably-built “Cookie Rush” collected flavor preferences alongside sign-ups.


From the[Skout case study](https://playably.ai/pages/skout) :


- 7× ROI
- 4× email conversion rate versus a standard form
- 200+ flavor survey responses
- 63% more email and SMS opt-ins


#### **The zero-party data angle**


A survey game answers a product question and builds a list at the same time. Playably campaigns hand those answers straight to the brand, and they segment future sends, which is worth more than the sign-up itself. More on that in[zero-party data collection](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/zero-party-data-collection) .


## **What the three have in common**


**Roshambo** **My Medic** **Skout**


Mechanic Play-to-win game Simulator with gated score Survey game


Discount offered None None None


Headline result 8.2% opt-in 3,659 opt-ins 7× ROI


Extra value Full-price buyers Version-to-version learning Product feedback


Three rules show up in all of them:


1. **The reward is the experience or the result,** not a code.
2. **The gate sits at the payoff,** right before the score, the match or the answer.
3. **The game is short.** Completion rates fall fast past about 60 seconds.


**Want a game built for your catalog?** Playably designs, builds and runs it, and there’s no discount code waiting at the end.[Book a 30-minute brief](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


## **Where this goes wrong**


Two honest failure modes.


**The game has nothing to do with the product.** A generic arcade game collects emails from people who like games. Michu’s litter-education game worked because it taught something about the product, alongside a 37% AOV lift.


**The game ends in a discount anyway.** Some gamified formats reveal a code at the end, which puts you back where you started with extra build time.


Playably builds each game around the product it’s selling, which is why the opt-in numbers above arrived with sales lifts attached.[See the Game Arcade](https://playably.ai/pages/games) .


## **Summary**


Playably is the best capture option for brands that care what the first order is worth, not just how many emails they collected.


The opt-in rate is the wrong scoreboard. What matters is what that subscriber costs you on their first order.


A 15%-off pop-up buying a 6% opt-in rate has already spent $12 on an $80 order it hasn’t made yet. A no-code game at 8.2% spends nothing. Judge capture tools on cost per full-price first order, and most discount pop-ups stop looking cheap.


## **Test one game against your pop-up**


Run a game alongside your existing pop-up for four weeks, split by traffic. Compare opt-in rate, first-order value and the discount given away in each path.

## **FAQ**


- **Does gamified email capture work without a discount?** Yes. Roshambo hit an 8.2% opt-in rate with no code attached.
- **What’s a good opt-in rate for a Shopify capture tool?** Roshambo’s case study cites 4.35% as the pop-up benchmark it beat at 8.2%.
- **Where should the opt-in gate go?** At the payoff, right before the score or result is revealed.
- **How long should a capture game be?** Under about a minute. My Medic’s completion rose to 48.9% after shortening.
- **What else can a capture game collect?** Zero-party data. Skout gathered 200+ flavor responses alongside sign-ups.
